title: Installation & First-Time Configuration
description: Install Git across operating systems and configure identity, default branch names, line endings, and editors.

blocks.content:
## Verifying and Installing Git

Check if Git is already installed on your system by opening a terminal:

```bash
git --version
# Example output: git version 2.44.0
```

If Git is not installed:
- **macOS**: Run `xcode-select --install` or `brew install git`.
- **Linux (Ubuntu/Debian)**: Run `sudo apt update && sudo apt install git`.
- **Windows**: Download and install Git from [git-scm.com](https://git-scm.com) or run `winget install --id Git.Git -e --source winget`.

## Configuration Scopes

Git stores configuration options at three distinct levels:

1. **`--system`**: Applies to every user and all repositories on the machine (`/etc/gitconfig`).
2. **`--global`**: Applies to the current operating system user (`~/.gitconfig` or `~/.config/git/config`).
3. **`--local`**: Applies specifically to the current repository (`.git/config`). Local overrides global, which overrides system.

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["1. Local Repo (.git/config)\nHighest Priority"] --> B["2. Global User (~/.gitconfig)\nStandard Setting"]
    B --> C["3. System (/etc/gitconfig)\nFallback Default"]
```

## Essential First-Time Settings

Set your name and email address immediately. These credentials are baked permanently into every commit you create:

```bash
# Set your public author name
git config --global user.name "Alice Chen"

# Set your email (match your GitHub/GitLab account email)
git config --global user.email "alice@example.com"
```

### Recommended Best-Practice Settings

```bash
# Set default branch name for new repositories to main
git config --global init.defaultBranch main

# Set default text editor (e.g. VS Code, nano, vim)
git config --global core.editor "code --wait"

# Ensure pull rebase behavior (cleaner linear history)
git config --global pull.rebase true
```

## Inspecting Your Configuration

To view all active settings and see exactly which configuration file set each value, use `--show-origin`:

```bash
git config --list --show-origin
```

To check the value of a specific single key:

```bash
git config user.name
# Output: Alice Chen
```

blocks.question: Which command sets your author email for all repositories on your user account?
blocks.explanation: The '--global' flag writes configuration to your user profile (~/.gitconfig), making it the default for all repositories you work with.

blocks.question: If a setting is defined in both ~/.gitconfig (--global) and .git/config (--local), which value takes precedence?
blocks.explanation: Git uses a cascading hierarchy: local repository settings override global user settings, which override system-wide defaults.
